Question: Why did JD Vance flee from military service after a measly 4 years, when Tim Walz retired after 24 years of service?

Question: Can a letter along with pictures be sent to a judge to show the results of an eviction case where she sided with the tenants?

Question: What happens if the buyer can’t pay the full amount of the closing cost? I’m buying a house. My closing cost is $14,000, but I only have $7,000. What can I do?

Question: I am the power of attorney, but my parents’ house is in a reversed mortgage and they have both passed away. Can I keep the house?
Answer: If you can pay for it you can buy the house from the estate. Your Power of Attorney ended when the Maker(s) died. It’s of zero use now. All that matters now is who is the Executor of the Estate? Because THAT is who will decide what happens to the house. The reverse mortgage is now due in full - principal, accrued interest, and any other fees required. The estate will be given a short amount of time to pay the mortgage IN FULL. If you want to keep the house AND the Executor agrees, you will have to buy it from the estate. If you don’t have the cash or can’t get financed, the Executor of the estate will have to sell the property to pay the loan.

Question: Were US Army combat medics ever or colloquially known as corpsmen? Or is that strictly a naval thing?

Once assigned to a USMC unit, he becomes “Doc”. After he deploys with his unit, he can be “pinned” and earn his “Devil Doc” status.

Question: Can you rent a house to another person while you are also the tenant? So for example there is a house which you have rented for 1500 dollars but you rent it to another person for 1700 dollars. Is it illegal?

Question: What should I do if my tenant dies and I do not have any information about his legal heir?
Answer: You follow your jurisdiction’s laws covering a tenant abandoning the premises. In my US state, since we KNOW he’s dead, we simply remove his property from the unit and store it securely for 30 days. We must send a notice to him at his last-known address, advising him that his property is in storage. Then we just move along and get the property cleaned up and re-rented. If his heirs show up within the 30 day mandatory storage period, they can pay the fees to get his property. If they won’t, or they don’t show up, at the end of the 30 days, we dispose of it however we wish - sell it, dump it, give it away, etc.
